From: James Li <james.li@montclaire.health>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@montclaire.health
Subject: Request: exception to latency SLA for private VPC peering

Hi Jordan,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. We're close on procurement but hit a blocker with the SLA language for the Private deployment. Our network team is asking that we carve out latency guarantees for traffic that traverses our VPC peering to a managed transit partner (we have a third-party overlay between our on-prem colo and the cloud VPC).

Concise ask: can Redwood agree to exclude end-to-end latency measurements that are demonstrably caused by customer-controlled peering, transit providers, or on-prem network maintenance? In practice this would be an exclusion clause so Montclaire isn't held to latency uptime credits when the root cause is our network or upstream carrier.

Attached is a redline of the SLA section from procurement with suggested language and a sample network trace showing an interconnect spike last month.

Would appreciate a quick confirm or suggested alternative. We're targeting signature by Friday so we can start the onboarding window in January.

Thanks,
James Li
Director, Cloud Ops
Montclaire Health

Subject: Re: Request: exception to latency SLA for private VPC peering

Hi James — thanks for the clear note and for the redline. I copied Lauren (AE) and Vivek (Solutions) so we can review the ask from both commercial and engineering perspectives.

Initial reaction: Redwood is open to limited shared-responsibility carveouts, but we need a concrete operational definition (how to prove the root cause) and a mitigation path (fallback models or capacity guarantees) so end-users remain protected. Two quick questions:

- Is Montclaire expecting the exclusion to apply automatically when you detect packet loss/latency before the peering hop, or will you provide incident reports that certify the root cause?
- For billing/credits: do you want latency credits to be replaced by an availability SLA for the control plane, or simply a no-credit carveout?

I'll circle back after we sync with engineering. If possible, can you share the vendor contact for the transit provider so Vivek can engage their NOC if needed?

Best,
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Request: exception to latency SLA for private VPC peering — tech readout

James / Jordan — quick tech readout from our infra side. Thanks for the packet capture; it helped a lot. High level:

- Redwood's Private deployment measures token latency at the model runtime ingress point inside the customer's VPC (we instrument the agent that terminates TLS on the private control plane).
- If packets are dropped or delayed upstream of that ingress — e.g., at a transit partner, customer-managed peering, or on-prem WAN — the latency we observe will reflect the customer infra.

Given that, we can do a scoped carveout if the following are in place:
1) A mutually agreed RCA process: Montclaire provides a vendor incident ID or NOC report within 48 hours.
2) Network boundary proof: the customer provides traceroutes/packet captures showing the increased RTT/packet loss with timestamps.
3) Fallback policy: When a carveout is invoked, Redwood will automatically route new sessions to a lower-latency hosted fallback model (subject to capacity) for up to a 72-hour remediation window.

Operational notes: the carveout must be timeboxed per incident, and repeated incidents above an agreed threshold (e.g., >3 in 30 days) revert to standard SLA and an escalation to joint remediation. Also recommend we add a short clause saying we won't apply credits for latency-related incidents validated by the RCA above.

I can draft the legal-friendly wording if you want. If you can confirm the transit provider + sample incident ID we can validate the example trace.

— Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference

Attachments: none

Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 08:47:00 -08:00
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: James Li <james.li@montclaire.health>
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.com, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com, procurement@montclaire.health
Subject: Re: Request: exception to latency SLA for private VPC peering — proposed commercial language

James — per Vivek's notes we've drafted language that attempts to balance your ask with our need to avoid unbounded exclusions. Key points in the suggested text:

- Definition: "Customer-controlled network path" will include customer VPC peering, third-party transit providers, and any customer-managed on-prem WAN.
- Evidence: customer must submit an incident ticket or NOC vendor report and packet-level traces; Redwood will have 48 hours to validate.
- Consequence: for validated incidents Redwood will not apply latency credits; Redwood will offer a hosted fallback and engineering assistance for up to 72 hours.
- Repetition cap: if validated carveouts exceed 3 incidents in any 30-day window, the carveout is suspended and the parties will enter a joint remediation plan.

I've attached a redline that inserts this wording into Section 4.2 of the SLA. If this looks acceptable, I can have Legal produce a final contract amendment and we can route for signature.

Next steps (suggested):
- Montclaire confirms transit vendor and shares one or two historical incident IDs (so we can validate the process)
- Procurement confirms if the repetition cap is acceptable or if you prefer a different threshold
- I will then push a final amendment for signature

Thanks —
Jordan

Attachments: montclaire-sla-redline-20261201.pdf (updated with carveout language)

Subject: Re: Request: exception to latency SLA for private VPC peering — accepted terms with small ask

Jordan / team — thanks for the quick turnaround and thorough proposal. Montclaire agrees to the RCA steps and the repetition cap, but procurement asked for one modification: when a carveout is validated and the fallback hosting is used, Montclaire requests a "no-cost" failover window (i.e., Redwood will not charge additional per-token overage for sessions routed to hosted fallback for the first 24 hours of the incident). Beyond 24 hours standard billing applies.

Rationale: we want to avoid double-billing during incident bursts while we remediate the underlying network. If you can accept that I believe Procurement is ready to sign.

Sample incident ID for validation: TRANSIT-20261114-0456 (included in the packet capture). Transit provider: Nimbus Transit Solutions (noc@nimbus.net).

Thanks,
James

Montclaire Health

James — that's reasonable. Redwood can accept the 24-hour no-cost hosted failover for validated incidents, with the following clarifications to be captured in the amendment:

- The 24-hour no-cost window applies only to traffic routed to Redwood-hosted fallback models triggered by a validated carveout; if the customer requests additional capacity beyond normal committed throughput during that window, overage rates will apply.
- Validation must follow the 48-hour RCA process Vivek outlined.
- All other SLA credit calculations remain unchanged; the carveout is limited to latency-credit exclusion and the one-time 24-hour failover credit per validated incident.

I'll have Legal produce an amendment and route for signature against deal D-2026-1147. Lauren will coordinate next steps on procurement signature and onboarding dates.

Appreciate the pragmatic approach here — looking forward to getting you onboarded.

Best,
